drafts.walkScript: Look at the order in line 63. He had 'unfastened a rope' back on line 59. So now he ties the boat up. On line 63, 'smartly' tells you he went at speed.
Read on from 'tolerable' in line 66. Lines 66 and 67 go on: 'but not handsome enough to tempt me'. So it means only just good enough. Putting up with things belongs to a different word, tolerant.

Lines 48 and 49 say a door was mistaken "In the agitation and half darkness". Line 4 says "We're in the new house"; lines 53 and 54 show a missed supper. A mistaken door and a missed supper show an upset, muddled arrival after dark. So "agitation" means the upset and muddle of arriving late at night. The darkness is the time, not the feeling; nothing is stirred, and the room comes later.

Line 44 says "Somebody has to keep the goal." Line 43 says "I'm not shifting out of there", so "there" means the goal. The speaker is staying put in goal and will not leave it. So "shifting" means moving away from a place. Stacking jumpers is line 42, and nobody changes shape or works a turn at a job.
